model: FCFE at cost of equity for a bank (engine route, net debt zero, preferred deducted)

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement (XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation = $317M); already expensed inside noninterest expense, so it is added back into the 'EBITDA' line and deducted again via sbc_pct_path (house basis) to keep the street/house band meaningful
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,221.6M common outstanding at 2026-06-30 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding / us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding, Q2-26 10-Q) plus ~5.5M dilutive awards (Q2-26 diluted weighted 1,239.0M vs period-average outstanding ~1,233.8M) = 1,227M. Held flat: buybacks are a use of FCFE (distributed), so shrinking the count as well would double-count them; SBC is charged in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: 10.5% = 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.15 x ERP 5.0% + ~0.5% for regional-bank CRE/deposit-run tail risk. Single rate across scenarios; scenario risk is carried in the flows (bear has a credit-cycle provision spike), not charged twice in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: n/a for a bank model -- occupancy cost is inside noninterest expense, already in pre-tax income.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house bank precedent (HBAN, NTRS, STT, NAB.AX). Routing table says residual income on tangible book; FCFE-at-CoE is used for consistency with the other US banks and because TFC book carries $18.3B goodwill+intangibles and AOCI swings, and the business is paying out >100% of earnings during the CET1 glide. Mapping: revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (XBRL InterestIncomeExpenseNet + NoninterestIncome; the CSV has no revenue tag for this bank). 'ebitda_margin' = (pre-tax income after provision for credit losses + SBC) / revenue; sbc_pct deducts SBC back out (house). D&A = 0 (immaterial, inside expense). 'capex_pct' = equity retained to fund balance-sheet growth = revenue growth x (tangible common equity / revenue ~1.94), i.e. the capital needed to hold CET1 flat as RWA grows. cash_tax_rate = effective tax rate (FY2026 guide ~14.5%, tax-credit investments; ramps to 17%). Flows are pre-preferred-dividend, so preferred stock ($5,411M carrying value at 2026-06-30) is deducted once in equity_bridge; deposits and bank borrowings are operating funding, so net_debt = 0. FY0 is TTM to 30-Jun-2026 so the flows start on the same date as the share count (H1-26 buybacks already out of the count). Base TTM revenue: FY2025 20,319 (14,423 NII + 5,896 nonII) - H1-25 9,886 + H1-26 10,417 = 20,850. TTM pre-tax 6,806 = 32.6% of revenue (34.2% incl. SBC add-back); Q2-26 run-rate 34.5%. last_fcf = TTM net income 5,470 (pre-preferred) as the FCFE proxy before retention -- OCF is not usable for a bank (deposit and trading flows).
inputs.tangible_book_check: Common equity 58,684 (64,095 total - 5,411 preferred) - goodwill 17,125 - other intangibles 1,130 = TCE 40,429 = $33.10/share on 1,221.6M; price 46.28 = 1.40x P/TBV.
inputs.excess_capital_note: CET1 10.9% at 30-Jun-2026 vs ~10% target by end-2027 implies ~0.9% x ~$420B RWA = ~$3.8B excess. Half ($1.9B) is credited in equity_bridge; the other half is left as a buffer against Basel-endgame/AOCI re-proposal risk.

equity_bridge.note: us-gaap:PreferredStockIncludingAdditionalPaidInCapitalNetOfDiscount, Q2-26 10-Q (2026-06-30); flows are before preferred dividends (~$300M/yr)
CET1 10.9% (Q2-26) gliding to ~10% by end-2027 per management; ~$3.8B excess on ~$420B RWA, 50% haircut

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 revenue guidance (+3.5-4%) and nominal-GDP-type balance-sheet growth; historical CAGRs are distorted (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-1.7%) diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR (+4.5%): equity shrank on AOCI losses (2022 rate shock), the FY2023 $6.1B goodwill impairment, and $1.0B+ preferred redemptions plus accelerating buybacks, while the 2024 TIH sale converted an operating business into capital returned. Equity CAGR is not a usable compounding rate here.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue (NII + noninterest income) FY2022 19,973 -> FY2025 20,319 (+0.6% 3yr, continuing-operations basis as restated after the TIH insurance sale). 5yr revenue CAGR not computed: FY2020-21 noninterest income includes the insurance brokerage now sold (FY2021 9,290 vs FY2022 5,660 restated), and FY2024 includes the -$6.65B securities repositioning loss (noninterest income -813). EPS from CSV (basic): FY2020 3.11, FY2022 4.46, FY2025 3.87; FY2023 was -1.09 (goodwill impairment). FCF CAGRs are null by design: bank OCF swings with deposit and trading flows and is not a cash-flow base. SBC ($317M, 1.6% of revenue) is small and stable; no SBC-vs-FCF divergence issue.

base.margin_rationale: Year 1 ~ Q2-26 run-rate (pre-tax 33.9% ex SBC add-back): revenue +3.5-4% guide, expense +1.75%, NCO ~55bps. Then ~1.6pp of operating leverage over five years from the auto/marine run-off and expense discipline, implying ROTCE ~15% -- the low end of management's 16-18% long-term target, not the target itself.
base.capex_rationale: Retention = growth x TCE/revenue (1.94) so CET1 holds flat; the one-off CET1 glide to 10% is credited separately in equity_bridge.

bull.margin_rationale: Lyons executes the commercial/payments pivot; fee income keeps compounding near 10%, efficiency ratio improves ~4pp, ROTCE reaches ~17-18% (management's long-term range).

bear.margin_rationale: Southeast recession in year 2: CRE office and consumer losses push NCOs to ~110bps (provision ~+$1.6B), NII falls with rate cuts and the auto run-off, revenue -1%. Retention stays elevated in year 2 (buybacks paused to rebuild capital) despite no growth. Margin recovers to only 34% (ROTCE ~13%): NIM permanently lower after the mix shift.

scenario_narratives.base: Truist grows revenue ~4% (guide 3.5-4% for FY2026) as fee income compounds and NII grows slowly through the deliberate exit from auto/marine/RV lending. Expense discipline adds ~1.6pp of pre-tax margin over five years; ROTCE settles around 15%, below the 16-18% long-term target. Credit stays near the guided ~55bps NCO. Excess CET1 above the 10% target is returned, half of it credited.
scenario_narratives.bull: The new CEO's commercial/payments strategy works: fee businesses keep growing ~10%, commercial loan growth accelerates in the Southeast, and the efficiency ratio improves ~4pp, delivering ROTCE in the 17-18% range and ~5% revenue growth for three years.
scenario_narratives.bear: A regional downturn hits in year 2: CRE (14% office) and consumer credit push charge-offs to ~110bps, revenue shrinks 1% as rate cuts and the auto run-off compress NII, and buybacks pause to rebuild capital. Recovery is to a structurally lower ~13% ROTCE.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 default, matching the regional/custody-bank precedent (HBAN, NTRS): high interest-rate sensitivity, a CEO transition (Lyons from 1-Sep-2026), a ~$28.9B CRE book with 14% office, and a >100% total payout ratio during the CET1 glide leave a fatter left tail than an operating company with net cash.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Truist is valued as a bank: free cash flow to equity is earnings after the capital retention needed to keep CET1 flat as the balance sheet grows, discounted at the cost of equity, with preferred deducted and deposits treated as operating funding (net debt zero). The question is whether a ~15% ROTCE franchise at ~1.4x tangible book is cheap; at a 10.5% cost of equity a 15% ROTCE growing 3-4% justifies roughly 1.6-1.7x tangible book.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: CRE ($28.9B, 14% office) and consumer losses; each +10bps of NCO on ~$320B loans is ~$320M pre-tax (~$0.22/share of annual earnings)
Rate path / NIM: NII guided only +1-1.5% for FY2026 as the auto/marine run-off trades yield for quality
Capital rules: Basel III endgame or AOCI recognition could remove the excess-capital credit and slow buybacks
Execution under new CEO Michael Lyons (from Sept 2026); the 16-18% ROTCE target is not assumed in base
Tax: the ~14.5% effective rate relies on tax-credit investments; base ramps to 17%
